_comment: Keys the aura-settings plugin may read and write on behalf of the apps and the agent, plus the settings catalogue the console and Android screens render from. GENERATED from aura-schema (make schema) — edit aura-schema/, not this file.

groups.title: Model
groups.description: Which model answers, where it runs and how much context it gets.

groups.title: Voice
groups.description: Speech in and out: the recogniser, the voice, and how a spoken turn ends.

groups.title: Agent
groups.description: How far a goal or a single turn may run on its own.

groups.title: Tools
groups.description: Which toolsets new sessions start with.

groups.title: House
groups.description: jarvis-core, the house service behind the rooms, devices and automations.

groups.title: Homelab
groups.description: The services on the LAN JARVIS reaches: search, images, telemetry, workflows, guests and GitLab.

groups.title: Messaging
groups.description: The chat platforms JARVIS answers on. A platform only ever answers the ids you list; an empty list means nobody.

groups.title: Network
groups.description: Addresses and origins the apps and the adapter bind to and accept.

groups.title: Console
groups.description: The web console's own login and phone pairing.

groups.title: Backups
groups.description: Where the nightly backup lands and how many are kept.

groups.title: System
groups.description: Images, timezone, updates and the Hermes back-ends the adapter proxies.

groups.title: HUD
groups.description: How the HUD is arranged; JARVIS may rearrange it unless locked, and your own arrangement always wins.

goals.max_turns.doc: Turns a standing goal may take before it parks

approvals.mode.doc: When the approval door opens: manual = every gated tool asks, smart = an auxiliary model decides for you, off = never

model.default.doc: The model every conversation runs on

tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled.doc: Stop a turn whose tool calls loop without progress

tool_loop_guardrails.loop_caps.max_web_s.doc: Web searches one turn may make

hud.mode.doc: Which preset the map is in: overview (everything as glyphs), task (the current work's panels open), focus (one panel open, the rest glyphs) or ambient (the reactor and a minimal strip).

hud.lock_layout.doc: Lock layout: while on, JARVIS may not move, resize, open or close panels.

hud.reduced_transparency.doc: Replace glass blur with solid panels: follow the system setting, or force on/off.

hud.reduced_motion.doc: Shorten or drop panel and reactor animation: follow the system setting, or force on/off.

hud.sync_layouts.doc: Apply a layout chosen on one device to the other devices of the same surface kind.

hud.layouts.doc: Saved arrangements per surface and activity; written by the window manager, not by hand.

hud.car_navigation.doc: Where a route Jarvis finds is driven in the car: Jarvis's own map on the car screen, with its turns said aloud, or a navigation app (Organic Maps, Google Maps, HERE WeGo) in the car's app pane. Ask Jarvis to change it.

hud.car_speak_directions.doc: Say each turn of a route aloud on the car's speakers, timed from the car's speed so the words arrive before the turn. Ask Jarvis to change it.

hud.car_clock.doc: Where the car screen shows the time: in the top bar, in a small Clock panel, or not at all.

hud.car_voice.doc: Where a reply in the car is spoken from: the phone itself when it can keep up (auto), always the house, or always the phone. Spoken from the phone it needs no connection, so it does not break up on mobile data.

hud.car_speed_warnings.doc: Jarvis says to slow down, in the persona's words, when the car's average speed is well over the road's limit; the Speed panel shows it either way.

hud.car_speed_warn_over.doc: How many mph over the limit the car's average speed must be before Jarvis says anything.

hud.car_speed_full_over.doc: How many mph over the limit fills the Speed panel's bar; the words (safe, speedy, risky, dangerous, deadly) scale with it and the bar runs past full.

hud.car_speed_average_s.doc: Seconds of driving the Speed panel averages, so a moment's overtake is not a warning.

hud.car_speed_repeat_s.doc: Seconds before Jarvis repeats a speed warning, unless the speeding gets worse.

voice.reasoning_effort.doc: How long JARVIS thinks before answering a spoken question (car, phone, console mic). "none" is faster to the first word; a level that differs from model.reasoning_effort other than none makes a spoken turn re-read the conversation after a typed one.

voice.pronunciations.doc: How JARVIS says names it would get wrong, as written=spoken pairs separated by semicolons, e.g. "Siobhan=shi-vawn; Nguyen=win". Whole words, any case; the transcript keeps the written name.

voice.quiet_hours.doc: When JARVIS speaks softer and a little slower, as HH:MM-HH:MM in the house's time (it may wrap midnight); empty for never.

privacy.quiet_house.doc: One privacy switch: the house makes no call out on its own (sky downloads, a scheduled forecast, a trip's map region); what you ask for still works.

settings.description: The model every conversation runs on
OpenAI-compatible base URL of the model server the agent talks to.
Token context window the provider advertises.

The inference key of the model server: llama-swap in jarvis-models answers only this bearer, and Hermes, the adapter and the house gateway present it. Unset, llama-swap stays open to the host's containers.
Base URL of the llama-swap model router (model load/unload control).
Seconds a llama-swap request may take before it is abandoned (cold start is slow).

How long JARVIS thinks before answering. "none" turns thinking off; the levels above bound it. Unset, the model server decides, and on this hardware that means it can think past every task's time budget.
Model for reasoning-heavy work. Empty means the default model answers (no swap); naming another model asks JARVIS to load it first.
Model for writing and fixing code. Empty means the default model answers (no swap); naming another model asks JARVIS to load it first.
Model that reads images and screenshots. Empty means the default model, which serves vision_analyze on this deployment.

Model for JARVIS' side calls — compression, titles, the goal judge, the skill curator. Empty means the default model; a smaller model here only pays off if llama-swap can keep it resident alongside the default one.
Model the delegated subagents run on. Empty means they inherit the parent's model, which is the only zero-swap answer while one model fits.

Embedding model for retrieval, served by ROUTING_EMBEDDING_URL. Empty is the deployed position: the memory provider searches with SQLite FTS5 and needs no embeddings. llama-swap's qwen3-embedding-0.6b (on the CPU) is one to point at.
Base URL of a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint. Must stay on the LAN: a cloud embedding service would send memory off the house.
Largest batch of delegated subagents. A request for more than this many children is refused, not queued, so keep it above the size of an ordinary multi-part request; they all share one model server.
How deep delegation nests: 1 means a subagent cannot delegate, 2 lets a subagent run children of its own. Every level multiplies what the one model server answers at once.
Structured long-term memory behind the memory tools. 'holographic' is a local SQLite fact store in the JARVIS volume; empty keeps only MEMORY.md/USER.md.
faster-whisper model size for speech-to-text (baked into the image).
Piper voice the assistant speaks with (baked into the image).
Which engine Hermes speaks with: openai (the house voice service, Kokoro on the card) or piper (one voice, no GPU).
The voice service's OpenAI-shaped base URL, as Hermes reaches it on the compose network.
The model name the voice service answers to; it accepts one.
The voice Hermes' own speech uses (its platforms' voice notes): the default theme's, AURA's Kokoro stock voice; the console and the apps ask the adapter for the speaking persona's voice instead.
Piper voice the phone/desktop apps ask the pipeline to speak with.
Which speech service speaks: wyoming (Piper, the default), openai (a Kokoro-shaped /v1/audio/speech) or cosyvoice (the house voice service, Kokoro).
Base URL of the speech service when tts.engine is openai or cosyvoice; empty means the engine's own default port on this host.
Milliseconds of silence before a spoken turn is considered finished.
Whether the apps require holding a button to talk instead of open-mic.
How JARVIS says names it would get wrong, as written=spoken pairs separated by semicolons, e.g. "Siobhan=shi-vawn; Nguyen=win". Whole words, any case; the transcript keeps the written name.
When JARVIS speaks softer and a little slower, as HH:MM-HH:MM in the house's time (it may wrap midnight); empty for never.

How long JARVIS thinks before answering a spoken question (car, phone, console mic). "none" is faster to the first word; a level that differs from model.reasoning_effort other than none makes a spoken turn re-read the conversation after a typed one.
Turns a standing goal may take before it parks
Stop a turn whose tool calls loop without progress
Web searches one turn may make
When the approval door opens: manual = every gated tool asks, smart = an auxiliary model decides for you, off = never
Days a standing "always" approval lasts before JARVIS asks again. Every live one is listed under Approvals, where it can be revoked sooner.

Where shell commands and execute_code run: aura-bwrap = a bubblewrap sandbox in the container (no network, no environment, one scratch per task), local = the gateway process itself, with every credential it holds.
The directory a coding job is allowed to write in. The approval matrix resolves a tool's paths against it, and anything landing outside is a write beyond the workspace, which asks before it happens.
GPU temperature (°C) at which the watchdog raises an alert.
GPU temperature the alert clears under. Below the alert point on purpose: without the gap a card sitting on the limit alternates alert and recovered on every tick.
VRAM in use (%) at which the watchdog raises an alert.
VRAM percentage the alert clears under, with the same hysteresis as the temperature pair.
How long the watchdog stays quiet between reminders while a threshold is still crossed.
Hour (house local time) quiet hours begin. Scheduled digests and recovery notices hold until they end; a threshold alert still fires.
Where every shipped scheduled job delivers. Empty means the house companion; `telegram`, `discord` or `platform:chat_id` send it to a messaging platform instead.
Hour quiet hours end. Equal to quiet_hours_from means there are none.
Toolsets on for new sessions
Toolsets off for new sessions
Which image backend image_generate uses
Base URL of jarvis-core's Home-Assistant-shaped REST API (loopback when it shares the host).
Long-lived token for jarvis-core's REST API (the 'house').
Secret the emergency plugin and the house share: the house keeps a new emergency contact list only with the plugin's proof under it (T-1213). Empty: the house refuses every change to the list.

Where the house itself posts an emergency alarm (what, kind, time; no contact details) when the phone cannot send it: an ntfy topic or n8n webhook URL (T-1208). Empty: nothing leaves the house. The flow behind it should confirm with you before telling anyone.
jarvis-core base URL the console uses for the house pages.
jarvis-core access token the console and HUD present.
One privacy switch: the house makes no call out on its own (sky downloads, a scheduled forecast, a trip's map region); what you ask for still works.
SearXNG endpoint the web toolset searches through.
SearXNG instance secret (openssl rand -hex 32).

Local article-extraction service the web toolset reads pages through. The default is the compose service by name, so a stack works without an .env edit; there is no cloud fallback, so a wrong value fails naming this variable rather than rerouting anywhere.
Seconds to wait for the extraction service before giving up on a batch of URLs.
Whether web_extract may use the local extraction service. Off, the tool has no extract backend at all — which is the point: it must never silently reroute to a cloud provider.

The house's Photon geocoder, which place_search asks first for names and addresses near the car (jarvis-core compose `photon`, --profile geocode, with PHOTON_REGION set). None running is the ordinary case until one is built.

Whether place_search may fall back to the public Photon (komoot) and OpenStreetMap's Nominatim when the house's place index and Photon have no answer. On, the search words and a point rounded to about 100 m leave the house; the result says so. Off by default (T-0765): where the car is stays in.

Whether car_navigate, for the owner, has the house download the map region a route ends in when no offline map covers it (T-0979), so the car's map and turn-by-turn work there with no connection. On, Geofabrik hears that region's name (a state, a country), never the destination. Off, a region is downloaded only when asked for (map_region_download, or the phone's Maps settings).

An Overpass server place_search may ask for 'the nearest' of a kind (a cafe, fuel, a pharmacy) within 5 km of the car when the house's place index has none. Empty by default (T-0765): the kind and a rounded point would leave the house for a public one.
ComfyUI endpoint the image_gen plugin submits workflows to.
Whether to verify TLS when calling ComfyUI (the homelab's sits behind a self-signed front).
ComfyUI checkpoint name to load, when the workflow takes one.
Named ComfyUI workflow the image_gen plugin fills in (txt2img, qwen-image, or a path).
Negative prompt filled into the workflow when the caller gives none.
Sampler steps when the caller gives none; unset means the workflow's own default.
Classifier-free guidance scale; unset means the workflow's own default.
AuraFlow sampling shift for the Qwen-Image graph (ComfyUI's template value).
Diffusion model file for the Qwen-Image graph; empty means the plugin's shipped default.
Text encoder file for the Qwen-Image graph; empty means the plugin's shipped default.
VAE file for the Qwen-Image graph; empty means the plugin's shipped default.
Free VRAM (GB) required before a generation is submitted; below it the tool refuses with the fix named.
Seconds to wait for a ComfyUI prompt to finish.
Grafana base URL for GPU/telemetry reads.
Grafana service-account token.
Grafana datasource UID (or name) for the InfluxDB telemetry queries; empty picks the first.
Whether to verify TLS when calling Grafana.
InfluxDB base URL for telemetry reads; set, it is preferred over the Grafana proxy.
InfluxDB API token.
InfluxDB organisation the telemetry bucket lives in.
InfluxDB bucket Telegraf writes nvidia_smi into.
Measurement name the GPU exporter writes (nvidia_smi, dcgm, …).
Tag that identifies a GPU in the telemetry rows.
Field name for GPU utilisation.
Field name for VRAM in use.
Field name for total VRAM.
Field name for GPU temperature.
Field name for power draw.
n8n base URL the trigger plugin posts webhooks to.
n8n API key, when the instance requires one.
Whether to verify TLS when calling n8n.
user:pass for webhooks protected by basic auth.
'Name: value' header for webhooks protected by a header token.
Proxmox VE API base URL (guest control, owner-waived by default).
Proxmox API token id (user@realm!tokenname).
Proxmox API token secret.
Whether to verify TLS when calling Proxmox (self-signed certificates are common on PVE).

The house's DNS zone (home.example): every name under it is a homelab service the tools may reach and that is never the public internet. Empty: the zone GitLab is in (GITLAB_API_URL's host less its first label).
GitLab API base URL for the gitlab MCP server.
GitLab personal access token for the gitlab MCP server.
Whether the gitlab MCP server is started.
Seconds a read-only integration call may take.
Seconds a writing integration call may take.
Numeric id (or url-encoded path) of the JARVIS project on GitLab, so a merge request the self-extension loop opens can be looked up without guessing.
Working checkout of this repository the self-extension loop scaffolds into and pushes from. Every selfext tool is unavailable until it is a git work tree.
Git remote the self-extension branch is pushed to.
Branch a self-extension merge request targets. Never pushed to directly.
Prefix every branch the self-extension loop creates must carry, so a push can be told apart from a human's branch and refused if it is neither.
Seconds a git or test subprocess in the self-extension loop may take.
IMAP server hostname JARVIS reads mail from.
IMAP port (993 implicit TLS, 143 plain/STARTTLS).
Whether the IMAP connection is TLS from the first byte (port 993).
SMTP server hostname JARVIS sends mail through.
SMTP port (587 STARTTLS, 465 implicit TLS, 25 plain).
Whether to upgrade the SMTP connection with STARTTLS after greeting.
Mailbox login used for both IMAP and SMTP.
Mailbox password or app password. Least privilege: one mailbox, not an admin account.
Address outgoing mail is sent from; empty falls back to the mailbox login.
Base URL of the DAV server that carries contacts and files (e.g. https://cloud.lan/remote.php/dav). Calendars are set in the house (`calendar:` in jarvis-core's configuration.yaml), not here.
DAV login shared by the contacts and files plugins.
DAV password or app password.
Whether to verify TLS when calling the DAV server.
Path under the DAV base URL where address books live.
Path under the DAV base URL where the file share is rooted.
Jellyfin base URL for library browsing and playback control.
Jellyfin API key (Dashboard → API Keys). Read scope is enough for browsing.
Jellyfin user id whose libraries and resume list are read; empty picks the first user.
Whether to verify TLS when calling Jellyfin.
Plex server address for read-only browsing: https, or plain http only to a private address such as http://192.168.1.20:32400. No login, query or fragment in it.
Plex token, sent only to the server above in a header. Nothing is played or changed with it.
Whether the Telegram gateway platform runs. Off, a bot token alone cannot switch it on.
Telegram bot token from @BotFather. Read from the environment by Hermes' own adapter; never written into config.yaml.
Telegram user ids allowed to talk to JARVIS. Empty means nobody: the gateway default-denies when no allowlist is configured.
Telegram group/forum chat ids whose members may talk to JARVIS.
Telegram chat id proactive messages and cron output are delivered to.
Whether the Discord gateway platform runs. Off, a bot token alone cannot switch it on.
Discord bot token. Read from the environment by Hermes' own adapter; never written into config.yaml.
Discord user ids allowed to talk to JARVIS. Empty means nobody: the gateway default-denies when no allowlist is configured.
Discord channel id proactive messages and cron output are delivered to.

What an unlisted person's direct message gets while NO allowlist is set: 'pair' offers a code the owner must approve, 'ignore' drops it silently. Once a platform has an allowlist, a stranger is dropped either way — Hermes will not answer unknown senders with pairing codes. Neither reaches the model.
Whether the inbound webhook platform runs, so n8n and CI can turn an event into a JARVIS turn.
Port the inbound webhook listener binds inside the container.
HMAC secret every inbound webhook must sign its body with. Without it the route refuses the request.
Address the stack's published ports bind to: the host's LAN address, reached from outside over WireGuard (the name predates the 2026-10-27 move to the LAN and is kept for compatibility).
Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the adapter/API directly.
Comma-separated origins jarvis-core admits (its own CORS allow-list).
Comma-separated origins allowed to open the HUD websocket.
URL the phone's pairing QR carries (how a phone reaches the adapter).
Adapter base URL the apps talk to.
Bearer key the apps present to the adapter.
Interface the adapter's HTTP server binds to.
Port the adapter's HTTP server listens on.
Comma-separated browser origins the adapter admits directly.
Seconds an adapter->Hermes request may take (a cold model start is slow).
Which backend an app targets (used by the phone to pick a host).
Secret that authorises minting a permanent phone-pairing token.
Console password in plaintext (hashed in memory, never written).
Console password as an scrypt$ hash line (nothing recoverable).
Override path where a browser-chosen console password is stored.
The console's https address; passkeys are bound to it. Empty: no passkeys, password only.
Minutes a browser's console session may sit unused before it must sign in again.
Voice pipeline name the HUD asks jarvis-core for.
Host path the nightly backup tarball lands in.
How many nightly backup tarballs to keep.
age public key (age1…) the nightly backup is encrypted to; unset, no backup is written.
Host path of the age private key file, mounted read-only for the weekly restore drill.
Host path of the second location each encrypted backup is copied to (another disk or a NAS).
Container registry the images are pulled from.
Image tag the compose stack pulls (the pipeline writes the short SHA here).
Image tag of the CosyVoice shim the compose stack pulls (built on its own tree, deployed by name so an app rollback leaves the voice alone).
Host directory holding the CosyVoice 3 weights, outside the deploy directory the pipeline rsyncs with --delete.
Container timezone (stamps logs and drives cron times).
Whether an app checks for and installs updates on its own. On: the desktop shell downloads in the background and installs on quit, never with a surprise restart.

Accelerator the desktop shell registers to start a turn from any window. Separate from voice.push_to_talk, which is the on/off switch: read as one setting, writing 'false' to switch push-to-talk off registered a hotkey named 'false'.

Accelerator the desktop shell registers to show the island with its typing line focused, from any window. Not a bare Ctrl+K: registered globally that would take the chord from every browser and editor. A key another app owns is logged and the tray says it is not available.

Accelerator the desktop shell registers to dictate into the focused window: hold it and speak, let go and what the adapter heard is typed where the cursor is (once, on release). Empty is off. It needs a modifier, and a chord the push-to-talk or typing key already is is not registered. Typing needs input_automation on for that desktop.
Loopback URL of the Hermes API server the adapter proxies (port 8642).
The Hermes API server key the adapter presents (port 8642).
The key the adapter presents to the model manager in jarvis-models (port 8001); unset, the manager listens on its own loopback only and the Models panel is off.
Loopback URL of the hermes-serve backend the adapter relays (port 9119).
The hermes-serve dashboard session token (port 9119).
Model name the adapter reports for the apps' /v1/models listing.
Log level the adapter's process logs at.
Bearer key the apps present to the adapter's front door.
Which preset the map is in: overview (everything as glyphs), task (the current work's panels open), focus (one panel open, the rest glyphs) or ambient (the reactor and a minimal strip).
Lock layout: while on, JARVIS may not move, resize, open or close panels.
Replace glass blur with solid panels: follow the system setting, or force on/off.
Shorten or drop panel and reactor animation: follow the system setting, or force on/off.
Apply a layout chosen on one device to the other devices of the same surface kind.
Saved arrangements per surface and activity; written by the window manager, not by hand.

Where a route Jarvis finds is driven in the car: Jarvis's own map on the car screen, with its turns said aloud, or a navigation app (Organic Maps, Google Maps, HERE WeGo) in the car's app pane. Ask Jarvis to change it.
Say each turn of a route aloud on the car's speakers, timed from the car's speed so the words arrive before the turn. Ask Jarvis to change it.
Where the car screen shows the time: in the top bar, in a small Clock panel, or not at all.

Where a reply in the car is spoken from: the phone itself when it can keep up (auto), always the house, or always the phone. Spoken from the phone it needs no connection, so it does not break up on mobile data.
Jarvis says to slow down, in the persona's words, when the car's average speed is well over the road's limit; the Speed panel shows it either way.
How many mph over the limit the car's average speed must be before Jarvis says anything.
How many mph over the limit fills the Speed panel's bar; the words (safe, speedy, risky, dangerous, deadly) scale with it and the bar runs past full.
Seconds of driving the Speed panel averages, so a moment's overtake is not a warning.
Seconds before Jarvis repeats a speed warning, unless the speeding gets worse.

The activity view: while the browser or the desktop is being driven, a live tile shows the page, the action and a reduced screenshot when a tool's result carries one, redacted before it leaves the container. Off, the aura-activity plugin emits nothing and no frame is captured at all.

Panel.description: One panel in a layout: a stable id, its content type, optional placement.
Panel.title: Panel

Rect.description:
A panel's placement in Floating mode, as fractions of the surface (0..1).

Ignored in Tiled/Focus/Ambient, where the tree decides. Fractions rather than
pixels so a layout saved on one screen size still means something on another.
Rect.title: Rect

Split.description: An interior node of the Tiled tree: two children side by side or stacked.
Split.title: Split

layout_document.description:
The saved arrangement of one surface for one activity.

``tree`` is the tiling tree (or ``None`` for an empty/ambient layout); every
leaf must name a panel in ``panels`` and no panel id may repeat, so a surface
never has to render a reference to a panel that does not exist.
layout_document.title: LayoutDocument
